member.name: M:BR.Adi.Interop.NativeMethods.AdiEnableWmi(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Enables or disables the WMI (Windows Management Instrumentation) support for ADI functions.
member.param: Boolean that specifies whether to enable or disable WMI. If this parameter is true, WMI is enabled and certain methods are performed via WMI: for example the CPU internal temperature of an APC620 and PPC700 is read via WMI (ACPI). If the parameter is false, WMI is disabled and all methods are performed by the ADI driver.
member.returns:
true indicates success; false indicates failure. To get extended error information, call the method.
Error CO_E_NOTINITIALIZED (0x800401F0) is returned, if the COM library is not initialized.
member.remarks:
WMI is the Microsoft implementation of Web Based Enterprise Management (WBEM), which is built on the Common Information Model (CIM), a computer industry standard for defining device and application characteristics so that system administrators and management programs can control devices and applications from multiple manufacturers or sources in the same way.
The WMI support is enabled or disabled for the calling application only.
An enabled WMI support is valid only until the system is rebooted. After system start the WMI support is disabled.
Note: AdiEnableWmi is supported on Windows XP and Windows 2000 only. The COM library must be initialized with Windows function CoInitializeEx before AdiEnableWmi(true) is called. CoUninitialize must be called after AdiEnableWmi(false). You can find the description of these functions in the MSDN Library.
APC620, PPC700: Requires ADI driver version 1.30 or higher.
PP100/200, MP100/200: Requires ADI driver version 2.00 or higher.

member.summary: Downloads data from a file to the device.
member.param: Points to a that specifies the name of the file to read.

Points to a callback function which will be called to indicate the download progress in percent. The download process is cancelled when the callback function returns false. Specify null if no callback is required.

Error Code Description
ERROR_BUSY Another download is already active (from a different thread of the application).
ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY Not enough memory is available to load the file.
ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED The data for the specified data type may not be overwritten.
ERROR_INVALID_DATA The ADI DLL detects invalid data (for example the file is empty or the device ID in the XML header does not match the device or the file version is too low) or different data is found at verify.
ERROR_HANDLE_EOF Not all requested data can be read from the file.
ERROR_CANCELLED The callback function returned zero.
ERROR_CRC The ADI driver detects invalid data (for example a firmware file is specified instead of a key configuration file at dataType KeyCfg or a firmware file for a different device at dataType FPGA_FIRMWARE) or the file is damaged (checksum is wrong).
ERROR_REVISION_MISMATCH An incompatible firmware version was downloaded, for example SDLR FPGA 1.04 to an Automation Panel 900 which has a SDLR FPGA version less than 1.00.
ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION A file shall be downloaded to a data area, which is just in use (e.g. by a concurrent upload).
member.remarks:
The latest files for BIOS, firmware and settings are available on device specific upgrade disks. You can update (= download) BIOS, firmware (even with old format) and settings also with the device specific upgrade disks. You can download these disks from the B&R homepage [ http://www.br-automation.com ].
The download may pause for a time during some flash memory operations (for example at erase). The application-defined callback function will not be called during this.
Warning: Stop an active watchdog during download with . Otherwise a PC reset may happen if the specified watchdog cycle is shorter than the time required for long Flash memory operations!

PP100/200, MP100/200: Requires ADI driver version 2.00 or higher.
